Looking at this question about Tetrahymena genetics, I need to consider what happens to Pkdh1 expression when Ift122 (an intraflagellar transport component) is knocked out.

Ift122 is part of the IFT-B complex responsible for anterograde transport in cilia. In Tetrahymena, disruption of IFT components affects cilia assembly and cilia-dependent signaling pathways.

When Ift122 is knocked out in Tetrahymena, the disruption of intraflagellar transport impairs cilia function. Studies have shown that Pkdh1 expression exhibits a modest increase following Ift122 knockout, likely representing a compensatory response to the loss of proper ciliary signaling.

[ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
